title: Do Transaction Prices Reflect Visual Preference? A Diagnostic Study with Multimodal Language Models
title_zh: 交易价格是否反映视觉偏好？一项基于多模态语言模型的诊断研究

paragraphs.en: 提出MarketImage诊断框架，研究交易价格能在多大程度上恢复多模态模型的视觉偏好信号。 Existing visual preference evaluation relies on costly human annotations or preference reward models, whereas online marketplace transaction prices are readily available and reflect real purchasing behavior, offering potential low-cost supervision. However, transaction prices conflate visual preferences with non-visual factors such as provenance, demand, and competition, making aggregate accuracy insufficient to distinguish model errors, unreliable price signals, and protocol confounds. To address this identifiability challenge, we introduce MarketImage, a diagnostic framework that identifies when transaction prices reflect visual preferences, where they fail, and whether multimodal language models can recover human-supported visual preference signals. MarketImage comprises three components: (i) MarketImageArt, 266 six-image comparison sets with transaction prices and price-blind human rankings; (ii) MarketImageLens, a tie-preserving protocol that partitions 3,990 within-set image pairs into price-human agreement, conflict, and price-tie regions while separately auditing presentation-order effects; and (iii) MarketValuator, six elicitation methods spanning direct comparison, independent scoring, budget constraints, and multi-agent aggregation to evaluate signal recovery by static visual scorers and three multimodal language models. Experiments show that only 24.2% of image pairs have a non-tied price direction, of which 34.7% agree with the human majority. Within this region, HPSv2 leads at 66.4% Recoverable Accuracy; Qwen's budgeted and aggregated variants trail baselines, while GPT interface gains remain statistically unresolved. Thus, transaction prices encode recoverable visual preferences only under limited conditions and should be treated as uncertain proxies rather than ground truth.
paragraphs.zh: 提出MarketImage诊断框架，研究交易价格能在多大程度上恢复多模态模型的视觉偏好信号。现有的视觉偏好评估依赖昂贵的人工标注或偏好奖励模型，而在线市场的交易价格易于获取且反映真实购买行为，有望提供低成本的监督信号。 然而，交易价格将视觉偏好与来源、需求、竞争等非视觉因素混杂在一起，使得总体准确率不足以区分模型错误、不可靠的价格信号与实验协议造成的混淆。 为应对这一可识别性难题，我们提出MarketImage，一个诊断框架，用于判定交易价格何时反映视觉偏好、在何处失效，以及多模态语言模型能否恢复有人类支持的视觉偏好信号。 MarketImage包含三个组件：(i) MarketImageArt，包含266组六图比较集，附带交易价格与价格盲的人类排序；(ii) MarketImageLens，一种保留平局的协议，将3,990个组内图像对划分为价格与人类一致、冲突和价格平局三个区域，同时单独审计呈现顺序效应；(iii) MarketValuator，六种引出方法，涵盖直接比较、独立打分、预算约束和多智能体聚合，用于评估静态视觉打分器与三个多模态语言模型的信号恢复能力。 实验表明，仅有24.2%的图像对具有非平局的价格方向，其中34.7%与人类多数意见一致。 在该区域内，HPSv2以66.4%的可恢复准确率领先；Qwen的预算约束和聚合变体落后于基线，而GPT接口的增益在统计上尚无定论。 因此，交易价格仅在有限条件下编码可恢复的视觉偏好，应被视为不确定的代理指标而非真实标准。
